kit.name: Arena Move
kit.summary: Top-down movement: one avatar per player, joystick or tilt steering, dash, wall bounce and body bumps.

accel.description: How fast velocity reaches the stick direction, px/s².

friction.description: Velocity decay per second when the stick is released (0 = ice, 20 = instant stop).

collidePlayers.description: Avatars push each other apart (needed for bump/steal mechanics).

dashButton.description: Controller button id that dashes; '' disables dashing.

dashPower.description: Dash speed as a multiple of `speed`.

input.description: Steering source: phone joystick or phone tilt.

tiltSensitivity.description: Tilt gain: phones are rarely tilted fully, so a modest tilt reaches top speed.

avatarScale.description: Avatar size multiplier (bigger = easier to bump, harder to dodge).

dashShove.description: A dashing avatar hits others this many times harder (shove rivals into hazards: knockouts).

shoveStunSec.description: Seconds a dash-shoved victim can't steer (it slides). Teammates are never stunned.

callout.description: Namespace for the headline events the TV calls out (<callout>.ringout, .crumble, .overload, .core.pass, .paint.tally); '' = off.

ringOut.description: RING OUT mode: the arena is a round floating platform of floor tiles that crumbles inward ring by ring; anyone off the platform falls out and respawns in the centre.

ringRadius.description: RING OUT: platform radius at the start, px.

ringTile.description: RING OUT: floor tile size, px (one crumble ring is one tile wide).

ringShrinkTo.description: RING OUT: the platform crumbles (evenly from 30% of the round to 6 s before the end) down to about this radius, px.

ringOutPoints.description: RING OUT: points to the last player who touched a rival (within ringCreditSec) when that rival falls off.

ringFallPenalty.description: RING OUT: points lost for falling off (never below zero).

ringSurvivePoints.description: RING OUT: points to everyone still on the platform when a ring drops.

ringComebackPoints.description: RING OUT: comeback: a player in last place (behind everyone else) scores this when they respawn after a fall.

ringCreditSec.description: RING OUT: a touch this recent earns the ring-out credit.

respawnSec.description: RING OUT: seconds out after a fall before respawning in the centre.

respawnInvulnSec.description: RING OUT: after respawning, can't fall or be bumped for this long, s.

ringCrumbleEventKind.description: RING OUT: timeline event kind (exact) that crumbles the next ring right away. '' = off.

overload.description: OVERLOAD mode (hot potato): one player holds an unstable core; touching a rival passes it; when its hidden fuse runs out the holder loses overloadPenalty and everyone else gets overloadReward; then a new core goes to a random player.

overloadCores.description: OVERLOAD: cores live at once (at most one per two players: 4 players and 2 => two hot potatoes).

overloadFuseMin.description: OVERLOAD: shortest fuse, s (each core gets a random fuse between min and max; it pulses faster as it burns).

overloadPenalty.description: OVERLOAD: points the holder loses when the core detonates (never below zero).

overloadReward.description: OVERLOAD: points every other player gets on a detonation.

overloadAssistPoints.description: OVERLOAD: extra points, on a detonation, for whoever handed the core to the holder (on top of overloadReward).

overloadClutchPoints.description: OVERLOAD: points for passing the core while it is critical (its last 3 s): a clutch pass.

overloadSafePoints.description: OVERLOAD: every 5 s, everyone not holding a core gets this many points (holding costs you).

overloadPassImmunitySec.description: OVERLOAD: after passing the core you can't be given it back for this long, s.

overloadHolderSpeed.description: OVERLOAD: top speed multiplier of the core holder (keeps the chase fair).

overloadStunSec.description: OVERLOAD: the holder is stunned this long by the detonation, s.

overloadEventKind.description: OVERLOAD: timeline event kind (exact) that burns the current fuse down to a few seconds. '' = off.

paint.description: PAINT mode (territory): the floor is a tile grid; moving paints tiles in your team colour (own colour without teams); dashing paints a burst; tile share scores every paintEverySec and the final tally counts paintFinalMul times.

paintPoints.description: PAINT: points a tally pays for owning the whole floor (split by tiles you painted).

paintFinalMul.description: PAINT: the final tally at the buzzer pays this many times more.

paintBurst.description: PAINT: a dash paints a square of (2b+1)² tiles around you (1 => 3×3).

paintUnderdog.description: PAINT: players on the team (or player) behind on score dash-splash one size bigger (3×3 => 5×5): a comeback rubber band.

crates.description: CRATE CRASH mode (turns physics on): every player owns a square platform zone stacked with physics crates. Knock rivals' crates out of their zone (dash, bump, or a barrel blast from world.props) for crateKnockPoints; every crateTallySec you score crateStandPoints per crate still standing in your zone; the final tally pays crateFinalMul times.

cratesPerZone.description: CRATES: crates stacked in each zone (players × this ≤ 36).

crateSize.description: CRATES: crate size multiplier (1 = 44 px box).

crateKnockPoints.description: CRATES: points for knocking a rival's crate out of its zone.

crateStandPoints.description: CRATES: points per standing crate at each tally.

crateFinalMul.description: CRATES: the final tally at the buzzer pays this many times more.

crateRefillEventKind.description: CRATES: timeline event kind (exact) that refills every zone to full right away. '' = off.

crateRefillSec.description: CRATES: every this many seconds each zone gets a lost crate back (the last-place zone gets two); 0 = never.

kit.name: Collect
kit.summary: Items pop up; grab them for points, or carry them home to bank (own baskets, carry limits that slow you and make noise, combo bonus for full trips). Golden items, bump-to-steal.

itemSprite.description: Sprite key for items (art resolved by the renderer).

maxItems.description: Most items on the field at once.

pointsPerItem.description: Points per item (on pickup, or at the goal in carry mode).

carryToGoal.description: Items are carried and only score when brought to the goal.

goalX.description: Goal centre X as a fraction of arena width (carry mode).

goalY.description: Goal centre Y as a fraction of arena height (carry mode).

carryMax.description: Most items one player can carry at once.

stealOnBump.description: Ramming a player steals one carried item (carry mode) or pointsPerItem points.

stealCooldownSec.description: After a steal the thief can't steal again, and can't be robbed, for this long.

goldenChance.description: Chance (0..1) that a spawned item is golden.

goldenMultiplier.description: Golden items are worth this many times pointsPerItem.

spawnArea.description: Where items appear: anywhere, or within spawnRadius of the arena centre (e.g. around a sleeping guard: the risky zone).

spawnRadius.description: Max distance of a spawn from the arena centre when spawnArea is 'centre', px.

homeBases.description: Carry mode: every player gets their own basket (kind 'base', in their colour, spread along the edges); loot banks only at your own basket.

bankBonus.description: Carry mode: extra points per item beyond the first banked in one trip (1 => 1, 3, 6 for 1, 2, 3 items): rewards greedy trips.

carrySlowdown.description: Carry mode: top speed lost per carried item, as a fraction (0.12 => 3 items = 64% speed).

carryNoise.description: Carry mode: extra noise per carried item, as a multiple of normal (guards hear you better: 0.6 => 3 items = 2.8x as loud).

goldenEventKind.description: Timeline event kind (exact) that drops one golden item next to the guard / arena centre: a mid-round jackpot. '' = off.

frenzyEventKind.description: Timeline event kind (exact) that fills the field with items at once (a loot frenzy). '' = off.

callout.description: Namespace for the headline events the TV calls out (<callout>.bank, .steal, .golden); '' = off.

teamBases.description: Carry mode, team games: one base per team (kind 'base', team-tinted, left and right edges); loot banks at your team's base, and bumps never rob a teammate. Overrides homeBases.

stealNeedsDash.description: Only a dashing avatar (arena-move dash) can steal or knock loot loose; ordinary bumps do nothing.

knockLoose.description: Carry mode: a steal knocks one carried item loose onto the floor (anyone can grab it) instead of handing it to the thief.

bankLabel.description: Popup reason when loot is banked (e.g. 'BANKED').

kit.name: Dodge
kit.summary: Telegraphed hazards (rain, sweeping walls, chasers, bullet rings) ramp up; survive, skim close for near-miss points.

hazardSprite.description: Sprite key for hazards (art resolved by the renderer).

pattern.description: rain: drops from above; sweep: walls with gaps; chase: slow homing hunters; ring: bullet rings from a point.

startRate.description: Waves per second at the start (scaled per pattern: sweeps and rings are bigger).

rampPerSec.description: Added to the wave rate every second.

maxRate.description: Cap on the wave rate, waves per second.

telegraphMs.description: Minimum warning before a hazard can hurt anyone (never below 400 ms). The block lengthens it per hazard when the slowest/largest avatar needs longer to escape.

onHit.description: What a hit does: eliminate the player, lose hitPenalty points, or stun for stunSec.

hitPenalty.description: Points lost per hit when onHit is losePoints (score never drops below 0).

stunSec.description: Stun length when onHit is stun, s.

invulnSec.description: Grace period after a hit (with stun: at least stunSec + 0.5 s), so no double hits.

survivePoints.description: Points for every surviveEverySec without being hit.

nearMissPoints.description: Points for an armed hazard passing close without hitting.

safeZones.description: Circles where hazards can't hurt you; they relocate every safeZoneShiftSec.

hitKnockback.description: Hits fling the avatar away from the hazard at this speed, px/s (0 = none). Comedy with slippery movement.

knockoutPoints.description: Points to whoever shoved (dash-bumped) the victim into a hazard within the last 1.5 s.

crumbleLastSec.description: Floor of tiles (kind 'tile') that crumbles from the edges inward in the final N seconds: tiles shake (props.crumbling), then drop; standing over a hole counts as a hit. 0 = no floor.

callout.description: Namespace for the headline events the TV calls out (<callout>.knockout, .crumble); '' = off.

kit.name: Race
kit.summary: Lane race: mash or hold to run, jump obstacles, hit speed pads, optional relay with baton passes; heats repeat.

laneCount.description: Lanes drawn on screen; players share lanes round-robin when there are more players.

trackLength.description: Length of one lap in track units (px of running at speed 1).

checkpointCount.description: Scoring gates per lap (each worth checkpointPoints).

relay.description: Each lap is two legs: runner 1 must hand the baton to runner 2 in the handoff zone.

batonPassButton.description: Controller button id that hands over the baton (relay).

obstacleDensity.description: Obstacles per lap = round(obstacleDensity * 10); identical layout in every lane.

boostPads.description: Speed pads per lap (same positions in every lane).

mashToRun.description: true: tap runButton (or swipe right) to run; false: hold runButton / push the stick right.

runButton.description: Controller button id used to run (tap or hold, see mashToRun).

jumpButton.description: Controller button id that jumps obstacles (swipe up also jumps).

runSpeed.description: Top running speed, track units per second.

mashPower.description: Speed gained per tap as a fraction of runSpeed (mash mode).

stumbleSec.description: Seconds a runner stumbles after hitting an obstacle.

padBoost.description: Speed multiplier from a speed pad.

padBoostSec.description: How long a speed pad boost lasts, s.

gateCycleSec.description: 0 = obstacles are always there. >0 = obstacles are laser gates that switch on and off on this cycle (each gate out of step with the next): only a live gate trips you, so time your run or jump it.

gateOnFrac.description: Share of each gate cycle the laser is live.

finishLine.description: Draw a finish line entity (kind 'finish') at the end of the track.

kit.name: Sneak
kit.summary: Creep past guards: moving makes noise, hold Tiptoe to stay quiet. Wake the guard and it stares; get caught moving and you lose points.

guardSprite.description: Sprite key for the guard (bear, grandma, cat...).

guardKind.description: sleeper: dozes until noise wakes it. patrol: walks a loop, sees ahead. watcher: stands still, sweeps its gaze.

noiseLimit.description: Noise a guard tolerates before it wakes.

noisePerMove.description: Noise per second of full-speed movement right next to a guard (falls off with distance).

noiseDecayPerSec.description: Noise a calm guard forgets per second.

hearingRadius.description: Movement farther than this from a guard makes no noise for it, px.

tiptoeButton.description: Controller hold/button id: while held, avatars creep (slower, ~silent, invisible to calm guards).

wakeDurationSec.description: How long a woken guard stays awake (after a short wind-up telegraph), s.

wakePenalty.description: Points lost by whoever woke the guard, and by anyone it then catches moving.

visionConeDeg.description: Full angle of the guard's vision cone, degrees.

visionRange.description: How far a guard sees, px.

daringPoints.description: Points per few seconds spent creeping close to a calm guard (0 = off).

onWake.description: What a woken guard does. stare: stands and catches anyone moving in its vision cone. chase: runs after the loudest player (the culprit) for chaseSec; a catch makes them drop everything they carry and tumble.

chaseSec.description: onWake 'chase': how long the guard chases before it gives up and plods home to sleep, s.

chaseSpeed.description: onWake 'chase': guard run speed, px/s (set it between a loaded and an empty player's speed so greed is risky).

callout.description: Namespace for the headline events the TV calls out (<callout>.chase.start, .caught); '' = off.

kit.name: Tug of War
kit.summary: Two teams haul a rope: mash, pull on the beat, or hold and manage stamina. Drag the knot over your line to win the bout.

mode.description: mash: tap to pull. rhythm: one pull per beat, scaled by timing. hold: hold to pull while stamina lasts. beat: rhythm-mash, every tap pulls but taps on the beat pull beatBonus times harder.

ropeLength.description: Distance the knot travels from the centre line to either team's win line and back, px.

forcePerTap.description: Rope speed one tap adds (px/s), averaged over the team so uneven teams are fair.

fatigue.description: Stamina lost per tap (mash/rhythm) or per second held (hold); 0 = tireless.

rhythmBpm.description: Beat tempo for rhythm mode, beats per minute.

suddenDeathAtSec.description: Sim second at which pulls get stronger (sudden death).

pullButton.description: Controller button / hold id used to pull (swipes also pull).

winPoints.description: Points to every member of a team that drags the knot over its line.

beatBonus.description: beat mode: the first tap inside a beat's window (±150 ms, latency-compensated) pulls this many times harder than a normal tap.

offBeatMul.description: beat mode: pull of an off-beat (or second same-beat) tap, and such taps cost 2.5x the stamina: mashing loses to rhythm.

surgeCombo.description: Beats in a row where every team member lands exactly one on-beat tap (no mashing) that trigger a SURGE (a big yank toward that team); 0 = off. beat/rhythm modes.

suddenDeathBpmMul.description: At sudden death the beat speeds up by this factor (rhythm/beat modes).

underdogBoost.description: Rubber band: the team behind on points pulls up to (1 + underdogBoost) times harder, scaling with the gap (full at 2 bouts behind). 0 = off.

swingEventKind.description: Timeline event kind (exact) that makes the knot lurch toward the team behind on points (e.g. 'bear-sneeze'). '' = off.

callout.description: Namespace for the headline events the TV calls out (<callout>.surge, .splash, .swing); '' = off.

kit.name: Draw & Judge
kit.summary: Everyone draws the prompt on their phone; an AI judge scores each drawing 0–10 with a roast.

prompt.description: What everyone draws (the AI fills it from the game's ingredients).
prompt.default: A cat who just became king

judgeStyle.description: Voice of the AI judge's roasts.

kit.name: Trivia
kit.summary: Multiple-choice quiz on the phones: answer fast for bonus points. Questions are AI-written about the game (or the players).

questions.description: AI-filled. Empty: the block asks the host for a 'trivia-gen' judgement and falls back to a built-in bank.

pointsFast.description: Points for a correct answer in the first half of the question's time.

pointsSlow.description: Points for a correct answer after that.

aboutPlayers.description: Ask the generator for questions about the players themselves (names in the payload).

kit.name: Ball Sport
kit.summary: A physics ball and two goals (2v2 car-soccer / pinball football) or free-for-all keep-away. Dash into the ball for a power shot; it banks off walls. Needs arena-move for movement.

mode.description: goals = two goals on the left/right walls (teams: team 0 defends the left, team 1 the right; free-for-all: whoever touched the ball last scores in either goal). keepaway = no goals: whoever touched the ball last scores keepAwayPoints every keepAwayEverySec.

ballSize.description: Ball size (1 = radius 24 px, a bit bigger than a player; 2 = a giant beach ball).

ballBounce.description: Ball restitution: 0.4 = heavy, 0.85 = default lively, 1.1 = superball.

ballMass.description: Ball mass relative to a crate (0.35 default: players punt it far; 2 = a heavy medicine ball).

ballDamping.description: How fast the rolling ball slows (0 = never stops, 0.4 default).

goalSize.description: Goal mouth height, px (arena is usually 720 tall).

goalDepth.description: Goal depth from the wall, px: the ball scores once its centre is inside.

goalPoints.description: Points to the scorer (the scoring side's last toucher).

assistPoints.description: Points to every other player on the scoring team.

behindBonus.description: Comeback: extra points for a goal scored by the side (team, or player in free-for-all) that is behind on score ("COMEBACK GOAL!").

kickPower.description: Extra px/s a DASHING player adds to the ball on contact (a power shot).

kickoffReset.description: After a goal the ball returns to the centre and players to kickoff spots, frozen for kickoffSec.

kickoffSec.description: Freeze after a kickoff reset, s.

keepAwayPoints.description: keepaway: points per tick to whoever touched the ball last.

multiballEventKind.description: Timeline event kind (exact) that drops an extra ball in (max 3 balls). '' = off.

callout.description: Namespace for headline events (<callout>.goal with data.moment 'goal', .multiball); '' = off.

enabled.description: Rigid-body physics on (default true when world.physics is present). Players become round bodies; bumps transfer momentum and spin.

gravityX.description: Sideways pull on loose props (ball, crates, barrels) in px/s² (top-down default 0). Non-zero tilts the arena: things slide that way; players feel a gentle drift.

gravityY.description: Downward (+) / upward (-) pull on loose props in px/s² (top-down default 0). E.g. 400 = a sloped table everything rolls down.

restitution.description: Bounciness of every body and wall: 0 = dead thud, 0.6 = default, 1 = superball, >1 = pinball chaos.

friction.description: Contact friction: how much grazing hits make things spin and drag along walls (0 = ice, 1 = rubber).

linearDamping.description: How fast loose props slow down (0 = slide forever / floaty low-gravity feel, 1.2 = default, 5 = mud). Also scales how long knocked players slide.

angularDamping.description: How fast spinning stops (0 = spins forever).

playerMass.description: Player body mass relative to a crate (1). Heavy players bulldoze props and shrug off knockback; light players fly.

spin.description: Bodies rotate and spin on grazing hits (false = fixed rotation).

knockback.description: Multiplier on every player knock: bumps, dash shoves, bumper kicks and barrel blasts (2 = twice the chaos).

walls.description: Arena edges are solid bouncy walls for props (false = props can leave the arena).

bumperKick.description: Extra px/s a pinball bumper fires anything that hits it.

barrelPower.description: Blast strength of an explosive barrel (px/s at the centre, falling off to 0 at 220 px).

kind.description: ball = round bouncy body; crate = box that slides, rotates and spins; bumper = static pinball bumper that kicks; barrel = explodes with a radial blast when dashed into or slammed.

count.description: How many (all props together at most 40).

layout.description: Where they spawn: scatter (random, default), center (clustered in the middle), ring (evenly on a circle of `radius` around the centre), edges (along the walls), corners.

radius.description: ring layout: circle radius in px (default 200).

respawnSec.description: Barrels/balls that explode or leave come back at their spawn after this many seconds (0 = never; default 6).

notes: world.physics turns on rigid-body physics (planck.js): players become round bodies, bumps carry momentum and spin, props roll, bounce, topple and explode. Omit `world` for classic arcade movement.
Top-down arenas: leave gravity at 0 for a flat table; gravityY 200–600 = a sloped table everything slides down.
Feel presets: floaty / low gravity = linearDamping 0.2, restitution 0.9, arena-move friction 2; bouncy = restitution 1.0–1.2; heavy = playerMass 2, knockback 0.7; chaos = knockback 2, bumperKick 900.
world.props spawns balls, crates, bumpers (static pinball kickers) and barrels (explode when dashed into or slammed). Keep the total ≤ 40.
ball-sport needs no world.physics (it turns physics on itself); arena-move `crates` also turns it on.
theme.look picks the art: neon (glowing vector arcade), toybox (glossy plastic toys), cosmos (deep space), retro (pixel-art CRT). Set theme.sfxSet to the same id for matching music and sfx.
